observations.text: SP, due to a non-standardized briefing flow that did not follow the Briefing Guide Book sequence, did not present the mission profile and did not set the mission objectives. The briefing could not be completed without assistance, with the result that the IP had to take control of the briefing process and deliver part of the formation items himself. Further preparation of the Briefing Guide sequence is required.

SP, due to mission planning that did not address the forecast weather at the recovery time, did not identify the threat set for the sortie and briefed no alternate airfield criteria. The briefing could not be closed without assistance, with the result that the IP directed the planning and executed part of the mission profile presentation. The omissions were not recognized by SP until the IP raised them.

SP executed the mission briefing within the desired standards for the Training Section, covering the mission profile and the objectives to the formation's experience level. However, the objectives were stated only after the IP's verbal prompts and two Briefing Guide Book items were recovered with delay. Marginal performance for the block; independent statement of the mission objectives and briefing sequence discipline are expected to improve.

SP executed the mission briefing according to the Briefing Guide Book and determined the mission profile and objectives without IP prompting. The few omissions in the recovery sequence were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP's intervention. As wingman SP attended the debriefing flow and answered all questions on the flown profile. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP had full control of the briefing and debriefing process, determined the mission profile and objectives accurately and quickly and gave solid directives for their execution, without IP's intervention. CRM was made completely comprehensible to all formation members before briefing completion. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed mission planning, briefing and debriefing above the desired levels, presenting a fully developed mission profile with alternative ways of execution and named decision points, with negligible deviation from the Briefing Guide Book. In the debriefing SP covered every formation member's faults and analyzed objectives completion without prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to inadequate knowledge of the Briefing Guide Book structure, did not execute the formation briefing in the prescribed sequence and left the mission objectives and the knock-it-off criteria unstated. The briefing could not be completed without assistance, with the result that the IP had to take control of the briefing process and brief the formation items himself. Study of the Briefing Guide is required before the next sortie.

SP, due to a CRM breakdown in which the required behaviour - explicit role assignment - was not performed, did not make the lead and wingman duties comprehensible to all formation members before briefing completion. The briefing could not be closed without assistance, with the result that the IP re-briefed the roles and the join-up responsibilities. Formation members were unable to answer back the mission tasking until the IP intervened.

SP, due to a non-standardized briefing flow, did not cover the contingency part of the Briefing Guide Book, omitting the weather divert criteria and the lost wingman procedure. Both items were briefed only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the result that the omissions were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to schedule pressure to complete the syllabus event within the available window, did not plan the mission profile with alternative ways of execution and set objectives that did not match the formation's experience and mission difficulty level. The profile was reworked only after the IP's verbal indications, with the result that the mismatch was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP executed the mission briefing and debriefing within the desired standards, gave solid directives for the mission profile and confirmed comprehension by all formation members. However, two Briefing Guide Book items were briefed out of sequence and the debriefing of the wingman's faults was initially incomplete; both were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section; completeness of the debriefing and briefing sequence discipline are expected to improve.

SP had full control of the briefing and debriefing process and executed it accurately and quickly according to the Briefing Guide Book, determining the mission profile and objectives to the formation's experience and mission difficulty level. Solid directives were given for the mission profile, no IP prompting was required, and CRM was confirmed as completely comprehensible by all formation members before briefing completion. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed mission planning, briefing and debriefing with exceptional accuracy and above the desired levels, presenting alternative ways of execution, named decision points and divert criteria for the forecast weather. As wingman SP assisted the leader with notams, meteorological data and alternate airfields without interrupting the flow, and in the debriefing covered all formation members' faults and analyzed objectives completion. Above end of block MIF achieved.
